go-between-courier.desc: a doorstep courier in a gray jacket

red-herring-night-courier.desc: a night courier with a shoulder bag

steps.line: {boss-careless} stands at terminal T-07 at the start of the day, bots and drones queued below.
Below {boss-careless}, bots roll out in numbered order, and one tray has no recipient line.
The manifest screen shows a row for "T-07" with the recipient field blank.
{veteran-officer} sits on the bench by the bot bay in the afternoon.
{veteran-officer} eats beside {informant}, a tool roll on the bench between them, and nobody speaks.
{inside-officer} and {framed-officer} walk their patrol past the logistics hub door.
{boss-careless} calls "Morning, Sunny" from the window to {inside-officer} and says nothing to {framed-officer}.
{framed-officer} stops and scans the hub door alone.
{inside-officer} walks on past the hub door without scanning it.
{go-between-courier} knocks at tenement doors 5B and 9A in the morning, no parcel in hand.
{go-between-courier} waits outside 9A for two minutes, looking at the mat.
A delivery bot rolls past loaded with parcels, and {go-between-courier} takes none.
{go-between-courier} walks to the lift with empty hands.
A bot sets a parcel down at door 5B while {go-between-courier} waits by the stairs.
{go-between-courier} lifts the parcel, tilts it, and presses a thumb into the base corner.
{go-between-courier} steps into the lift with the parcel under one arm.
{desk-sergeant} stands at the station front screens at the start of the morning shift.
{desk-sergeant} points at a new wanted poster on the screens.
{desk-sergeant} posts the day's shift list to the station screens.
{go-between-courier} stops at the front screens and reads two posters, one and then the other.
{go-between-courier} walks out of the station lobby.
{red-herring-stall-neighbor} shouts one word after {go-between-courier} on the steps: "Rent!"
{red-herring-stall-neighbor} stands among the crowd at the front screens for ten minutes.
{boss-careless} walks through the leaf rows of the hydroponic farm in the evening, carrying a parcel.
{boss-careless} goes into the shed behind the leaf rows.
{boss-careless} comes out of the shed twenty minutes later with empty hands.
{night-stakeout-officer} stands at the farm gate at night, a paper cup on the ledge.
{night-stakeout-officer} points at a lit window in the shed behind the rows.
{night-stakeout-officer} watches a bot parked at the shed door, and nobody comes or goes.
{red-herring-night-courier} knocks at door 5B before dawn, a bag in hand, and waits.
{red-herring-night-courier} walks away down the hall, the bag still in hand.
A drone sets a parcel on the mat at door 9A while {go-between-courier} watches from the hall.
{go-between-courier} lifts the parcel off the mat at 9A.
{go-between-courier} sets an identical parcel down on the mat in its place.
{go-between-courier} steps into the lift carrying the first parcel.
{inside-officer} turns the patrol left past the hub window, ten blocks the long way round.
{framed-officer} says to {inside-officer}: "We turned left here yesterday."
{inside-officer} waves {go-between-courier} over at the gate and offers a ride.
{go-between-courier} shrugs at {inside-officer} and shakes {go-between-courier.his} head.
{go-between-courier} walks away from the hub gate on foot.
{framed-officer} stands at the gate with {framed-officer.his} back turned, reading the notice board.
{boss-careless} passes {inside-officer} a flat parcel through the hub window.
{inside-officer} takes the flat parcel and turns it over once.
{inside-officer} slides the parcel under {inside-officer.his} coat and walks on.
{red-herring-stall-neighbor} carries a heavy bag to the hub drop window late at night.
{family-caller-officer} stands at the drone bay late at night, comm in hand.
{family-caller-officer} reads a gold-edged sticker on a drone tray: "T-07."
{family-caller-officer} leaves the drone bay and heads for the lift.
{family-caller-officer} comes back to the bay fifteen minutes later with a takeaway bag.
{red-herring-night-courier} knocks at door 5B before dawn and waits, bag in hand.
{rookie-officer} calls out "Police!" and {red-herring-night-courier} runs down the stairs.
{veteran-officer} walks slowly down the stairs behind {rookie-officer}.
{veteran-officer} says to {rookie-officer}: "Ask again tomorrow."
Comm, one side: "Who? No, he gave badge 2207, from the station. Hold it by the door. Sounded like him."
{family-caller-officer} searches behind a bot rack in bay 14 in the early morning.
{family-caller-officer} lifts a parcel, and its base panel comes away over a hollow three centimeters deep.
A label under the base panel reads "terminal T-07."
{family-caller-officer} points at the label under the panel.
{boss-careless} stands at terminal T-07 across the bay, watching the bots roll out.
{boss-careless} shrugs when {family-caller-officer} holds up the parcel.
Comm, one side: "Not now, Mama. I found it."
{desk-sergeant} finds a crowd reading the station front screens in the morning.
{desk-sergeant} points at a gray bar sprayed across a wanted poster headed "Courier, doorsteps."
{desk-sergeant} posts a notice to the screens: "Poster defaced. Under repair."
{go-between-courier} stands at the screens for half a minute, looking at the gray bar.
{go-between-courier} walks out of the station lobby by the lift.
{rookie-officer} reads the hub scan log on a tablet at the front screens.
{rookie-officer} points {veteran-officer} at the hub door row, blank on six mornings.
{veteran-officer} says to {rookie-officer}: "Ask again tomorrow."
{desk-sergeant} posts the hub delivery log to the front screens.
{framed-officer} reads the delivery log: {framed-officer.his} own badge, "2207," beside two parcel pickups.
{framed-officer} says to {desk-sergeant}: "I was at the tenements Tuesday."
{desk-sergeant} shrugs at {framed-officer} and turns back to the screens.
{veteran-officer} stands by the bench at the bot bay in the afternoon.
{veteran-officer} waits by the bench for ten minutes, and nobody sits down.
{veteran-officer} unrolls a tool roll left on the bench, one wrench slot empty.
The bay rota on the wall has the mechanic's name struck out in pencil.
{veteran-officer} leaves the bot bay by the lift.
{night-stakeout-officer} and {rookie-officer} watch the bay door from the dark before dawn.
{rookie-officer} reads the shift board: {inside-officer} swapped onto the predawn slot with the desk sergeant.
{inside-officer} walks into the hub before dawn carrying a takeaway bag.
{inside-officer} and {boss-careless} talk low at the hub window.
Comm, one side: "Not tonight. No. Not tonight."
{night-stakeout-officer} and {rookie-officer} wait at the gate until first light, and no courier comes.
{rookie-officer} shrugs and pockets {rookie-officer.his} notebook.
{desk-sergeant} posts a notice to the station screens: "{framed-officer} suspended pending review."
{framed-officer} reads the notice on the screen twice.
{framed-officer} unclips {framed-officer.his} badge and hands it to {desk-sergeant}.
{framed-officer} walks out of the station without a word.
{burnout-officer} sits in a lobby seat in the afternoon and stays there.
{burnout-officer} eats from a carton in the lobby seat.
{burnout-officer} shrugs at {desk-sergeant} across the lobby.
{rookie-officer} searches the evidence shelf and finds an empty space where the parcel sat.
The shelf log shows the last signature, {inside-officer}'s, from the evening before.
{night-stakeout-officer} waits at the corner of the tenement hall before dawn.
{red-herring-night-courier} knocks at door 5B and waits, holding flowers and bread.
{extra:resident} opens 5B, and {red-herring-night-courier} hands over the flowers and bread with a hug.
{night-stakeout-officer} lowers the handheld scanner and stays at the corner.
{rookie-officer} waits at the stairs in the morning, out of sight of door 9A.
{rookie-officer} holds up a flat hand to {night-stakeout-officer}: hold.
{go-between-courier} knocks at door 9A and waits.
{go-between-courier} lifts a parcel off the mat at 9A.
{night-stakeout-officer} and {rookie-officer} arrest {go-between-courier} at door 9A, parcel and all.
{night-stakeout-officer} walks {go-between-courier} down the hall to the lift.
{desk-sergeant} restores the doorstep courier poster on the front screens, the gray bar gone.
{desk-sergeant} steps back as the crowd reads the restored poster.
{red-herring-stall-neighbor} stands at the front screens for ten minutes.
{red-herring-stall-neighbor} hands {rookie-officer} a receipt from the shop landlord.
{rookie-officer} reads the receipt aloud: "Rent paid through the month."
{rookie-officer} opens {red-herring-stall-neighbor}'s heavy bag and finds bolts of cloth inside.
{veteran-officer} and {rookie-officer} open the shed door behind the leaf rows in the morning.
{veteran-officer} finds crates of parcels inside, their base panels unscrewed.
{rookie-officer} finds a comm rig on a shelf with a call sheet beside it.
{night-stakeout-officer} stands at the shed door, watching the leaf rows.
{rookie-officer} carries the comm rig out to the cart.
{veteran-officer} points at a pile of label stubs, each one stamped "2207."
{desk-sergeant} reads the rig's call sheet: one call, "14:10," on the day of the stairwell chase.
A screen camera still shows {framed-officer} at the front screens that day, stamped "14:10."
{desk-sergeant} posts a corrected notice to the station screens: "{framed-officer} cleared."
{framed-officer} hands {desk-sergeant} {framed-officer.his} paper notebook.
{framed-officer} gives {rookie-officer} a small wave on the way past.
{veteran-officer} walks across the lawn in the early morning, a tool roll under one arm.
{informant} sits on a lawn bench in a new coat.
{veteran-officer} sits down on the same bench beside {informant}.
{veteran-officer} hands {informant} the tool roll from the bay bench.
{informant} tells {veteran-officer}: "T-07, every payday, 15:00. Bay three. I fitted the panels."
{night-stakeout-officer} stands at the hub gate in the afternoon, a paper cup on the ledge.
{boss-careless} steps up to terminal T-07 in midafternoon.
{boss-careless} passes {inside-officer} a flat parcel through the hub window.
{framed-officer} steps in and arrests {inside-officer} at the window.
{veteran-officer} and {night-stakeout-officer} arrest {boss-careless} at the terminal.
{framed-officer} and {veteran-officer} walk {inside-officer} and {boss-careless} to the lift.
{rookie-officer} pries up the base panels of the parcels in bay three.
{desk-sergeant} posts a closing notice to the station screens: "Case closed."
{framed-officer} walks up to the front desk with {framed-officer.his} badge back on.
{veteran-officer} passes {rookie-officer} the beat sheet.
{rookie-officer} shrugs, folds the beat sheet, and tucks it away.
The station 2 desk sends its hub scan log to the screens beside {desk-sergeant}.
{rookie-officer} reads down the station 2 scan list, row by row.
{desk-sergeant} says to {rookie-officer}: "Their log has the same gap."
{veteran-officer} walks across the lawn in the early morning, a tool roll under one arm.
{informant} sits on a lawn bench in a new coat.
{veteran-officer} sits down on the same bench beside {informant}.
{veteran-officer} hands {informant} the tool roll from the bay bench.
{informant} tells {veteran-officer}: "T-07, every payday, 15:00. Bay three. I fitted the panels."
{night-stakeout-officer} watches the logistics hub from the gate before the day shift.
{boss-careless} steps up to terminal T-07 at the same minute as on the first morning.
{night-stakeout-officer} waits at the gate, and nothing in the routine at the window changes.
{night-stakeout-officer} stands at the hub gate in the afternoon, a paper cup on the ledge.
{boss-careless} steps up to terminal T-07 in midafternoon.
{boss-careless} passes {inside-officer} a flat parcel through the hub window.
{framed-officer} steps in and arrests {inside-officer} at the window.
{veteran-officer} and {night-stakeout-officer} arrest {boss-careless} at the terminal.
{rookie-officer} pries up the base panels of the parcels in bay three.
{desk-sergeant} posts a closing notice to the station screens: "Case closed."
{framed-officer} walks up to the front desk with {framed-officer.his} badge back on.
{veteran-officer} passes {rookie-officer} the beat sheet.
{go-between-bartender} hands {extra:driver} a cup of tea first at the drone bay.
The line of bot handlers stacks up behind {extra:driver} while {go-between-bartender} waits.
{go-between-bartender} passes {extra:driver} a tray tag with no drone number on it.
{go-between-bartender} leaves by the service door at the same minute as the night before.
{go-between-bartender} and {go-between-courier} pass at the lift without a word.
{inside-officer-extra} sits a little apart from the others at the briefing.
Comm, one side, low: "Not here. Not here."
{inside-officer-extra} is the first one out of the briefing room.
{inside-officer-extra} asks {desk-sergeant} what station 1 is working on.
{go-between-courier} waits at the lift in the early morning and does not go through the gate.
{go-between-bartender} walks out from the hub to the lift.
{go-between-bartender} and {go-between-courier} trade a few short words.
{go-between-bartender} takes a tray tag from {go-between-courier}.
{go-between-bartender} goes back into the hub by the service door.
{boss-careful} walks through the tenement lobby at night with a bag in hand.
{boss-careful} unlocks flat 4C and goes inside.
A window on the fourth floor lights up after {boss-careful} goes in.
{night-stakeout-officer} stands at the hub gate in the afternoon, a paper cup on the ledge.
{night-stakeout-officer} watches a stand-in bot parked at terminal T-07, and no dispatcher appears.
{night-stakeout-officer} and {veteran-officer} wait at the gate while terminal T-07 stays unmanned.
{inside-officer} leaves the hub with a takeaway bag.
{rookie-officer} shrugs at the empty terminal and turns away.
{night-stakeout-officer} and {rookie-officer} search flat 4C and find bags and a comm rig.
{night-stakeout-officer} waits in the tenement hall in the dark before dawn.
{boss-careful} comes up the hall and unlocks door 4C.
{night-stakeout-officer} arrests {boss-careful} at the door of 4C.
{framed-officer} arrests {inside-officer} in the hall.
{rookie-officer} arrests {go-between-bartender} on the stairs.
{night-stakeout-officer}, {framed-officer} and {rookie-officer} walk all three of them to the lift.
{desk-sergeant} posts a closing notice to the station screens: "Case closed."
{framed-officer} walks up to the front desk with {framed-officer.his} badge back on.
{veteran-officer} passes {rookie-officer} the beat sheet.
{veteran-officer} waves once from the station door on the way out.
